questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angular speed of the Earth's rotation is $7.3 \times 10^{-5}$ rad·s$^{-1}$. Take the radius of the Earth at the equator to be $6400$ km. Then the ratio $(a_c/g)$ of the magnitude of the centripetal acceleration $a_c$ at a point on the equator to $g$, is of the order
questions.solution:
Given angular speed $\omega = 7.3 \times 10^{-5}$ rad·s$^{-1}$ and radius $R = 6400$ km $= 6.4 \times 10^6$ m.

The centripetal acceleration at the equator is:

$a_c = \omega^2 R$

$a_c = (7.3 \times 10^{-5})^2 \times (6.4 \times 10^6)$

$a_c \approx 53.29 \times 10^{-10} \times 6.4 \times 10^6 \approx 3.41 \times 10^{-2}$ m·s$^{-2}$

Taking acceleration due to gravity $g \approx 9.8$ m·s$^{-2}$, the ratio is:

$\dfrac{a_c}{g} = \dfrac{3.41 \times 10^{-2}}{9.8} \approx 3.48 \times 10^{-3}$

The order of magnitude of this ratio is $10^{-3}$.

Answer: $10^{-3}$
